name: History Narration
description: Short narrated history facts — events, people, oddities. Tone is curious and grounded; voice is the friend who reads a lot. Pair with archival footage, museum/artifact B-Roll, or stylized animated re-enactments (anime / cinematic cuts work for younger audiences).
exampleTopics: The Real Reason the Library of Alexandria Burned
What Pompeii's Final Day Actually Looked Like
How a Single Letter Started World War One
Why Genghis Khan Was Buried in Secret
The Plague Doctor's Mask — What It Was Really For
How the Aztec Calendar Predicted Eclipses
The Bizarre Logistics of Roman Roads
Why the Bronze Age Suddenly Ended
The Mystery of the Voynich Manuscript
What Daily Life Looked Like in Ancient Egypt
audienceHint: Casual history viewers who enjoy 5-10 minute deep-cuts — overlaps with audiences for Hardcore History, Real Civilizations, Drachinifel-style channels.
scriptContext: Anchor every piece to specific dates, names, and places — vague history slides into fiction. Cite the surprising primary-source detail wherever possible ('one letter from his secretary survives, and it says...'). Avoid contemporary political framing of ancient events.
